title: What If a Star Exploded 30 Light-Years From Earth?

scenes.text: What if a star exploded 30 light-years away? The sky would be the least of our worries.
A supernova that close would flood Earth with high-energy radiation.
That radiation could strip away much of the ozone layer, letting dangerous ultraviolet light reach the ground.
Ocean plankton and reef communities would be hit hard, and food chains could unravel.
Cosmic rays would stay elevated for hundreds or thousands of years, and climate could shift.
Relax. No star within 30 light-years is known to be about to explode. Betelgeuse is about 430 light-years away.

description:
What if a star exploded just 30 light-years from Earth?
Researchers say a supernova that close could damage the ozone layer and stress life on Earth, but no known star nearby is ready to blow.
